evidence.quote: | Ready, Some books when Transfer.holdsRecords books ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new rules are all in Tier 2. The file format, the checks and the order of refusals live in Summa.Storage.Transfer, and the import-only-into-new-books predicate does too. The Settings-page transitions are in Summa.Web.Engine.Accounting. The only Tier 3 change maps three kernel events to engine messages, and the HTML only shows the feature. Tiers 3 and 4 decide nothing.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with
model, [ OfferDownload(Transfer.fileName manifest (businessToday model ctx), "application/json", base64 file) ]

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added below Tier 4. The export time comes in through ctx.Now. The download goes out as an OfferDownload effect value, and the import is saved with the existing save/SaveBooks effect. Transfer.fs is pure: it uses the in-house Json module, with no System.IO or System.Text.Json. Each decision is pure and can be tested without effects, as the acceptance tests show.

evidence.quote: | _, _, false -> { model with Error = Some "This browser cannot offer downloads here." }, []

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Most facts are reused rather than copied: Exports.Classification, Exports.dataVersion, LocalSnapshot.encode/decode, Codec.dateText, and the Schema and Version literals. Two literals are copied, though. The exportedAt timestamp format is written once for writing (stamp) and again for reading (instantOf). The existing 'cannot offer downloads' sentence is copied from the neighbouring CPA-export branch (line 2838) instead of shared. Both pairs agree today but can drift.

evidence.quote: if n = 2m && statedContents document <> Some contents then

ARC-REV-01.rationale: What the books contain (contentsOf), the version-2 contents check and the version handling are all in Tier 2 Summa.Storage.Transfer. The preview text, including the singular/plural nouns, is built in the Tier 2 engine from Transfer.read's result. It does not recount the books. Tier 3 has no changes, and the HTML only binds the view value.

evidence.quote: | BooksTransferTextChanged v -> { model with BooksTransferText = v; BooksTransferPreview = transferPreview v }, []

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added. The preview is worked out purely from the pasted text and stored in the model. Contents counting and checking are pure functions in Tier 2. The only file read is IO.File.ReadAllText, and it is in a test, not production code.

evidence.quote: | Some(Json.Number n) when n <> 1m && n <> 2m -> Error $"Transfer files of version {n} cannot be read here."
if n = 2m && statedContents document <> Some contents then

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have one definition, contentsOf, and both export and read use it, so the preview shows the books' own counts. But the readable versions are not defined from the Version literal: 1m and 2m are written in the version guard and again in the contents check. These copies agree with Version = 2 now, but they will drift if the version changes. The duplicated timestamp format from change set 1 is still there.
